title: A newly created bot has no capability grant and cannot act
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Found by:** `chatticus-b88c0a` follow-on, during the `chatticus-2f2d87` live attempt
- **Blocks:** the product path to F-computer, and any customer whose bot is created this way

---

## What happened

A human in the enabled ACME workspace asked the bot:

> Use the household computer workspace to run `ls /workspace` and reply with the command output.

The bot answered that it **could not**. That was first read as the model *declining* to summon a computer — a prompting problem. The distinction matters, because "won't" and "can't" have completely different fixes and only one of them is worth spending a run on.

## The likely cause: no task grant

Capabilities are checked against a **task grant**. With none present, requests are denied with the literal reason `"no task grant"` (`python/src/chatticus/capability_sinks.py`), and workspace reads go through `gated_read_workspace` in the same module.

**`create_bot` issues no grants.** Its body contains no grant, capability, ceiling, or standing assignment. The ACME bot was minted through exactly that path, because the enabled workspace has no create-bot control (`chatticus-7622fd`).

So the bot most likely had no permissions at all, **correctly reported that it could not**, and was read as refusing.

## Why this is not lab-only

Any bot created through this path is in the same state: it exists, it looks fine in the roster, and it cannot act. If `create_bot` is reachable in any customer-facing flow — now or once `chatticus-7622fd` wires the UI to `POST /bots` — a customer gets a bot that answers questions and silently cannot do anything else.

A bot that appears healthy and is functionally inert is worse than one that fails loudly at creation.

## What is confirmed and what is not

**Confirmed:** the denial path and its `"no task grant"` reason exist; `gated_read_workspace` is grant-gated; `create_bot` assigns nothing.

**Not confirmed:** whether `request_computer_capability` is gated identically to `read_workspace`. It is classified as a browser-capability tool in `computer_capabilities.py`, but the grant check was not traced through to it.

**The decisive check is cheap:** read the ACME bot's actual grant state and the exact refusal wording. If the bot said something like *"I don't have permission,"* that settles it and no prompting work is warranted.

## Questions this raises

- What **should** a newly created bot be granted? Nothing until a human grants it, or a sane default within the organization's ceiling?
- Is `create_bot` missing the grant step, or is the grant meant to be issued separately and the UI never built it?
- Does the same gap apply to bots created through any other path?

## Done when

A bot created through the normal flow can either act within a default grant, or fails visibly at creation rather than appearing healthy and inert — and the ACME bot's refusal is confirmed as a grant denial rather than a model decline.

comments.text:
## Cheap check from code (2026-09-07) — do not tune prompts

`ControlPlane.create_bot` creates a `Bot` and `ensure_computer` only. It assigns **no** grant, capability, ceiling, or standing. HTTP `POST /bots` is the same path.

`CapabilityPolicy.evaluate` with `grant is None` denies with reason **`no task grant`**. Workspace sinks (`gated_read_workspace` / `require_granted`) go through that. `prepare_computer_tool` does **not** deny `request_computer_capability` when grant is None — so the labeled kernel F-computer summon can still run. The ACME UI `ls /workspace` path is the grant-gated one.

The human reports Ping said it **could not**, not that it would not. That is probably literal. Do not treat the log line "the model declining to summon the computer" as a prompting defect.

Live Dynamo grant dump and exact transcript wording: in flight. Prompting work is not warranted until that dump shows a grant *and* a refusal that is not `no task grant`.

## Cheap check done (2026-09-07) — exact wording is model prose

Grant state on the ACME `ls /workspace` turns: **none**. Ping exists. Human Task roster: **0** rows. Turn grants that do exist are later matrix turns, not these.

Exact reply (Dynamo channel messages / `turn.completed`):

> I can't run shell commands directly in the household workspace.

Unicode curly apostrophe in *can't*. **Not** the sink string `no task grant`.

| Turn | Grant | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First `ls` | absent | no tool calls; straight to that prose |
| Repeat | absent | `request_computer_capability` (`gate: workspace`) then `attempt.relinquished` then the same prose |

Do **not** tune prompts. `create_bot` still assigns no grant — that remains this card for later sinks. The ACME sentence was **not** a surfaced grant denial; it is `STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL` / incomplete computer path. Product order stays F-computer `RunTask` (`chatticus-82dab7c4-a44c-4e0e-ac19-51a0c7a12d09`) before create-bot grants.

comments.text:
## Thread closed: the capability has no tool (2026-09-07)

The live retest settles it. Same prompt, **computer running** in the customer account after `chatticus-82dab7`, same answer:

> I can't run shell commands directly in the household workspace.

That is literally true.

```
chromium_action_executor.py:16
_SUPPORTED_TOOLS = frozenset({"browser_open", "request_computer_capability"})
```

Two tools. No `run_shell`, `shell_exec`, `terminal_run` or `exec_command` anywhere in `python/src/chatticus/`. `request_computer_capability` with gate `workspace` is not a shell — the executor only opens Chromium, for the browser gate.

**Three hypotheses, all wrong:**

- *The model is declining* (prompting) — no; it called `request_computer_capability` on the repeat turn.
- *No task grant* (mine) — no; the gate is `if policy.grant is not None`, so absent grants **skip** the check rather than deny. Grants were genuinely absent, which is real and stays this card, but it was not the cause.
- *Escalation defect* (`STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL`) — no; escalation had nothing to escalate to.

**The bot was right and three diagnoses were wrong.** Worth remembering the next time a model reports an inability: it may be accurately describing the system.

**What stays on this card:** `create_bot` assigns no grant, capability, ceiling, or standing. Still true, still a real gap for later sinks, and now known **not** to be what produced this sentence.

**Terminal work moves to `chatticus-3e72dc`** as a build, not a verification.

comments.text: `7622fd` closed: UI and live `POST /bots` mint bots with **no grant**. This card is next. Composer 2.5 planning. Worktree to be named `/tmp/chatticus-5336ff-bot-grant` on `feat/5336ff-create-bot-grant`. Implementation not authorized until the plan picks **one** path: default grant at create, or fail visibly at create — not both, not prompt-tuning. The ACME `ls /workspace` sentence was not this bug; the gap is still a grantless healthy-looking bot.
